---
name: author-docs
description: >-
  Docs authoring guidance — tutorials, how-tos, reference, and conceptual guides in simplified ASD-STE100 — composed by author-prose for the docs kind. Reached only through author-prose, never matched directly.
allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, Skill
---

Invoke the `prose:docs-standards` skill before proceeding. If that skill is unavailable, report the missing skill and continue with the closest available workflow.

<objective>

Documentation — tutorial, how-to, reference, or conceptual guide — in which every sentence passes the simplified ASD-STE100 structural rules.

</objective>

<workflow>

1. Collect the doc set's established terms for every concept the text touches. The one-term-one-meaning rule binds new text to the existing vocabulary; introduce a new term only for a concept the set does not yet name.

2. Write in the register the content selects: imperative numbered steps for procedures, present-tense description for reference and concepts. Both registers obey `/docs-standards` `<additional_rules>` — the length caps, one instruction per sentence, active voice, simple tenses, condition before command, no modal hedging, no verbal "-ing" clauses, noun-cluster and paragraph caps, articles always present.

3. Apply the base catalog on top. Structural compliance does not excuse an ornate noun, an invented concept label, or a signposted conclusion.

4. Re-read each sentence against the caps before moving on — counting words in an overlong sentence after drafting the page costs more than splitting it in place.

</workflow>

<success_criteria>

- Every sentence is inside its cap, active, simply tensed, and article-complete.
- Procedures carry one imperative instruction per step with conditions first.
- Terminology is one-to-one across the doc set.
- Zero instances of any `/prose-standards` pattern.

</success_criteria>
